title: Timeouts and circuit breakers
description: Learn about timeouts and circuit breakers for fault tolerance. Understand how to prevent cascading failures in distributed systems.

data.text: Timeouts and circuit breakers are essential patterns for building resilient distributed systems. They prevent slow or failing dependencies from causing cascading failures and resource exhaustion.
Timeouts define how long to wait for a response before giving up. They prevent your system from waiting indefinitely on slow or unresponsive services.

items: Prevents threads from blocking indefinitely
Enables fallback behavior on failure
Protects against slow services
Different timeouts for different operations
Should be set based on SLA requirements

data.title: Timeout Levels
data.text: Set timeouts at multiple levels: client timeout, HTTP timeout, database timeout. Each should be appropriate for its context.
Timeout values should be based on your SLA requirements and realistic performance expectations.

items: Start with the 99th percentile of normal response times
Add a buffer for the timeout value
Shorter timeouts fail fast, longer timeouts tolerate slowness
Different operations need different timeouts
Monitor and adjust based on actual performance

data.text: Circuit breakers stop calling a failing service after a threshold of failures, allowing it to recover and preventing cascading failures.

items: Closed state—normal operation, requests pass through
Open state—requests fail fast, service is considered down
Half-open state—test if service has recovered
Prevents cascading failures
Enables graceful degradation

data.title: Why It Matters
data.text: Without circuit breakers, a failing dependency can consume all your resources (threads, connections) and bring down your entire system.

items.title: Closed (Normal)
items.description: Requests pass through normally. Track failure rate. If failure rate exceeds threshold, trip to open state.

items.title: Open (Tripped)
items.description: All requests fail immediately without calling the service. After timeout, transition to half-open to test recovery.

items.title: Half-Open (Testing)
items.description: Allow limited requests through. If they succeed, close the circuit. If they fail, return to open state.

items: Failure threshold—how many failures before tripping
Success threshold—how many successes to close the circuit
Timeout—how long to stay open before testing
Rolling window—time period for measuring failures
Exception types—which exceptions count as failures
Always set timeouts on all external calls
Use circuit breakers for all critical dependencies
Combine with fallback mechanisms for graceful degradation
Monitor circuit breaker state transitions
Configure appropriately based on service characteristics
Test circuit breaker behavior in failure scenarios

data.title: Don't Overuse
data.text: Circuit breakers add complexity. Use them for dependencies that can fail and where failure would be catastrophic. Not every call needs one.

items: Timeouts too long—resources tied up waiting
Timeouts too short—false failures, degraded experience
Circuit breakers too sensitive—trip too easily
Circuit breakers not sensitive enough—don't protect the system
Forgetting to monitor circuit breaker state
Not implementing fallback behavior
